# Notation and Conventions {#sec-notation}

Every chapter uses the symbols on this page rather than defining its own. When a chapter needs a
new symbol, it is added here in the same change. If two chapters ever use one letter for two
things, that is a bug in the book.

This book shares conventions with its siblings where the topics overlap:
[loss-functions-lab](https://ioannisantoniadis.github.io/loss-functions-lab/appendix-notation.html)
for losses, risks and likelihoods, and
[rl-for-llms](https://ioannisantoniadis.github.io/rl-for-llms/appendix-notation.html) for the
sampling distribution $q$ and the weight $w$. The section on resolved conflicts below lists every
place where this book departs from them, and why.

## Data and distributions

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $x \in \mathcal{X}$ | an input (feature vector); $x_j$ its $j$-th feature |
| $y \in \mathcal{Y}$ | a target: a class, a real value, a token |
| $d$ | the input dimension |
| $n$ | the number of training examples (the sample size) |
| $D = \{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ | a dataset; $D_{\text{train}}$ and $D_{\text{test}}$ when both appear |
| $X$ | the $n \times d$ design matrix |
| $p$ | the **target distribution**: the one the model will face. $p(x, y)$, $p(x)$, $p(y \mid x)$ |
| $q$ | the **training (sampling) distribution**: the one examples are drawn from. Same arguments as $p$ |
| $w$ | a **per-example weight**; under covariate shift, $w(x) = p(x)/q(x)$, the density ratio |
| $p(y)$, $q(y)$ | class priors under the target and training distributions |

## Learning

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\theta$ | model parameters |
| $f_\theta$, $\hat f$ | a model; a fitted model |
| $\ell(y, \hat y)$ | the per-example loss |
| $R(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim p}[\ell]$ | the risk under the **target** distribution |
| $\hat R(\theta)$ | the empirical risk on a sample |
| $R^\star$ | the Bayes risk: the lowest risk any predictor can reach (the floor of a learning curve) |
| $E_n$ | the expected test error after $n$ training examples: the **learning curve** |
| $\beta$ | the exponent of a power-law learning curve, $E_n \propto n^{-\beta}$ |

## Collection, labels and cleaning (Part I and II)

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $s(x, y)$ | the probability that an example drawn from $p$ is kept when the data is collected; then $q \propto s\,p$ |
| $W_h$, $S_h^2$, $S^2$ | in stratified sampling: stratum $h$'s share of the population, its variance, the overall variance |
| $\eta(x)$ | the clean posterior $P(y = 1 \mid x)$ under $p$ |
| $\tilde y$ | a recorded (possibly wrong) label, as opposed to the true $y$ |
| $\rho_0$, $\rho_1$ | class-conditional flip rates: $P(\tilde y = 1 \mid y = 0)$ and $P(\tilde y = 0 \mid y = 1)$ |
| $t_j$ | in confident learning, the average predicted probability of class $j$ among examples labeled $j$ |
| $r$ | the share of a column's values that is missing |
| $m(x)$ | the conditional mean of the transformed target, $\mathbb{E}[\log y \mid x]$ in [Changing the Shape](chapters/06-changing-the-shape.qmd#sec-shape) |
| $\hat\varepsilon_i$ | a training residual of a fitted model |

## The long-tail testbed (T2)

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $p_i$ | the probability of feature $i$ under the target distribution. Hutter (2021) writes $\theta_i$ |
| $\alpha$ | the Zipf exponent: $p_i \propto i^{-(\alpha+1)}$, as in Hutter (2021). Dohmatob et al. (2024) write $p_i \propto i^{-\beta}$, so their $\beta$ is this book's $\alpha + 1$ |
| $K$ | the support size, when the feature set is truncated for computation |
| $E^{\text{oracle}}_n$ | the error of the oracle coverage selector that labels features $1, \dots, n$: $\sum_{i>n} p_i$ |
| $M$ | the size of an unlabeled pool a selector may inspect |
| $m$, $D_m$ | the number of draws from a uniform stream, and the number of distinct features among them (the labels used when only new features are labeled) |
| $s$, $A$ | $s = \alpha + 1$ and $A = 1/\zeta(s)$, so that $p_i = A\,i^{-s}$ |
| $c$ | the constant in an asymptotic power law $E_n \approx c\,n^{-\beta}$ |
| $\zeta(s)$, $\Gamma$ | the Riemann zeta function $\sum_{i\ge1} i^{-s}$; the gamma function |

## The other testbeds

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $z$, $\Sigma$ | T1's latent Gaussian features and their covariance; observed $x = z$ or $x = e^{z}$ |
| $a$, $b$ | T1's regression coefficients: $\log y = a + b^\top z + \varepsilon$ |
| $u$, $u_0$ | T1's classification coefficients: $P(y = 1 \mid z) = \sigma(u^\top z + u_0)$ |
| $\varepsilon$ | a noise term, with standard deviation $\sigma_\varepsilon$ |
| $\phi$ | T3: the angle between student and teacher; the test error is $\phi/\pi$ |

## Transforms

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\lambda$ | the Box-Cox / Yeo-Johnson power parameter |
| $\sigma_\varepsilon$ | the noise standard deviation (for example of $\log y$ under log-normal noise) |
| $F_j$ | the cumulative distribution function of feature $j$ |
| $\Phi$ | the standard normal cumulative distribution function |

## Probability and information

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathbb{E}$, $\mathrm{Var}$ | expectation and variance; the distribution is written as a subscript whenever it could be either $p$ or $q$ |
| $\sigma(z) = 1/(1+e^{-z})$ | the logistic sigmoid; bare $\sigma$ is never a standard deviation in this book |
| $H$ | entropy; for the Markov text testbed (T4), $H$ is the entropy rate in nats per token |
| $\mathbb{1}[\cdot]$ | the indicator function |

All logarithms are natural.

## Resolved conflicts {#sec-notation-conflicts}

- **Class priors are $p(y)$ and $q(y)$, not $\pi_y$.** The sibling books reserve $\pi$ for
  policies. The lens of this book also makes the prior-shift correction read as what it is: a
  change from $q$ to $p$. SPEC v0.1 §8 claim 10 wrote $\pi_y$; that claim is restated in this
  notation.
- **Hutter's $\theta_i$ is $p_i$ here.** $\theta$ means model parameters in every sibling book,
  and in T2 the feature distribution *is* the target distribution $p$, which makes the
  comparison of $q$ with $p$ direct (as in Dohmatob et al. 2024, who also write $p_i$ and
  $q_i$).
- **$\sigma$ is the sigmoid, as in the siblings**, so noise scale is $\sigma_\varepsilon$.
- **$\beta$ is a learning-curve exponent here.** In rl-for-llms, $\beta$ is the KL strength;
  the two books never need both.

## Recurring visual devices

**Data cards** (`callout-tip`): every technique, generated from `scripts/technique_data.py`,
with the same eight fields in the same order: changes, assumption, what it does to the learned
function, which models care, fit on, failure modes, alternatives, checked by. The
[decision guide](chapters/15-decision-guide.qmd#sec-decision-guide) is assembled from them.

**Lever colors**, in every figure: representation blue, sampling distribution $q$ orange,
weights $w$ aqua, labels violet. Exact ground truth is drawn in black.
